narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your savings account status, your property ownership, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. 

Your lack of any known savings was the biggest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Most approved applicants have at least some savings, whereas you fall into the unknown or none category that the model associates with higher risk. 

Your ownership of real estate worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This is generally viewed positively compared to applicants with no assets. 

Finally, your very low installment rate of 1% of disposable income also helped your case, as it is well below the average of roughly 3% among those who were approved. This suggests you would have manageable payments relative to your income.

Unfortunately, the negative influence from having no savings outweighed these positive aspects. 

To improve your chances on future applications, focus on building verifiable savings over the next several months. Even modest, consistent deposits can demonstrate financial responsibility and may significantly strengthen your profile. Consider reapplying once you have established this positive savings history.
